doc.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022

title: Defining genius
summary: Genius means changing one's medium; ghetto genius went to hip hop.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: How do you define genius? I remember talking to Phil Woods who very honestly made the assessment of himself, that he was a craftsman not an innovator. And I wonder if, © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
well to get back to my original question, do you have a definition for yourself of a genius in any field?

Well it’s my definition, it won’t conform with the dictionary’s definition, but a genius to me is a person who makes his or her medium different from the way it was before them. You see? And I think a lot of the genius may have gone out of jazz when it became more bourgeois. I mean that ghetto genius that produced Charlie Parker, you know, and Bud Powell and Thelonious Monk now got lost to hip hop because we took the instruments away from the kids. So they made a music out of words. If that genius had gone into jazz we would have a different jazz you see. But I don’t know what to do about it, I mean I’m definitely I’m for all kinds of training programs in communities of people who are without resources. I’m for all of that. But I don’t know how we get that back.
